title: Gemba launch runway — KPI snapshot and ops checklist
body:
Context:
This is a working Gemba-style one-week launch simulator for a small-batch beta (500–2k weekly users) of a latency-sensitive feature. Purpose: validate KPI wiring, exercise escalation paths, and leave a compact checklist for on-call / launch commander.

Goals (week of simulation):
- Prove steady-state p95 latency < 280ms for 95% of requests under expected workload mix.
- Keep request error rate < 0.5% and availability > 99.5% across regions.
- Ensure cost per 1k tokens stays within target band (hosted plan) and identify top 3 optimization levers.

KPI snapshot (initial targets & current baselines):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms): target 80 / 220 / 450 — baseline: 92 / 310 / 840
- Thruput (requests/min): expected steady 130 RPM — observed 110 RPM on staging
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts): target < 0.5% — staging observed 0.9% (spike on model coldstart)
- Token cost (USD per 1k tokens): target 0.60 — baseline 0.72
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): target > 35% — baseline 18%

Owner mapping (quick):
- Launch commander: Maya Chen (product-ops)
- Runtime infra / scaling: Arjun Patel (platform-engineering)
- Observability & dashboards: Sophie Alvarez (observability)
- Customer incident lead (CS escalation): Priya Singh (customer-success)

Seven-day run simulation (high level):
Day 0 (preflight): smoke dashboards, confirm alerting thresholds, seed synthetic traffic patterns, validate canary route rules.
Day 1: small-batch ingress (5% of expected), observe latency distribution and cache priming. Validate rollback path.
Day 2: increase to 25%, enable cost telemetry retention. Run targeted perturbation (KV cache miss flood) and evaluate degradation.
Day 3: full-weekday peak simulation (75% traffic). Test autoscaling and burst policies. Trigger canary fault injection.
Day 4: ramp to 100% traffic for 1 hour then back off; measure tails and queuing.
Day 5: degrade model quantization profile to cheaper variant for 10% of traffic as a cost experiment.
Day 6: customer-facing load (real beta cohort). Collect quality signals (eval prompt set) + ops metrics.
Day 7: post-mortem dry run and Handoff doc for steady state.

Prelaunch checklist (must-pass before Day 1):
- [ ] Dashboard tiles validated: tokens/sec, token-cost, p95 latency, error rate, regional availability
- [ ] Alerts: p95 latency > 350ms (P1), error rate > 1% (P1), autoscale lag > 2min (P2)
- [ ] Canary route policy configured with auto-fallback to smaller model variant
- [ ] KV/prefix cache warmup script added to pipeline and smoke-run schedule created
- [ ] Cost meter in place for per-route token breakdown (billing tagging enabled)
- [ ] Support rotation scheduled (first 72h) and Slack channel #gemba-launch created

Gating thresholds & decision heuristics (quick):
- If p95 latency breaches 420ms for > 5 consecutive minutes: throttle non-critical routes, enable smaller model variant, notify SRE.
- If 5xx rate > 1.5% sustained for 10m: execute rollback to previous model version and route 100% away from canary.
- If cost per 1k tokens rises > 30% above target: limit model context window for non-critical requests and enable intermediate quantization.

Contingency playbook (short):
- Latency tail: enable per-route throttling -> increase batching window for non-interactive flows -> spin temporary dedicated capacity (if committed pool available).
- Cold starts: ensure warmed instances for top 3 LBs; if cold-starts persist, pin canary pool warmup.
- Observability gaps: flip to debug-level tracing for 10m for affected traces; keep retention short.

Telemetry & runbook links (quick hops):
- Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/launch/gemba-kpi (primary)
- Pager rota: https://oncall.redwood.ai/rota/launch-week
- Postmortem template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Launch+Postmortem+Template
- Incident Slack: #gemba-launch (alias to #oncall-ops)

Notes to self / open questions:
- Do we have per-route token tagging in the billing pipeline for dedicated tenants? (Arjun to confirm)
- Should we pre-stage quantized artifacts to avoid on-the-fly quantization during ramp? (Sophie: add as action)
- Plan a small user-sampled quality check pipeline (5% of requests) to run eval-prompts automatically and alert on degradation > 5% in pass-rate.

Post-launch ops handoff (brief):
- 72h playbook: maintain hourly check-ins, track KPI drift, freeze rollout if any P1 alert fires twice.
- 30-day follow-up: cost optimization retro, model quality calibration, and adoption telemetry review.

This is a working document: expect changes after first dry-run. Use this as the single source during the launch week. Add notes inline and append learnings to the Confluence sim page.

-- Maya
